**UNO – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | |---------|---------------| | **Deck** | Standard UNO set (108 cards):
• 90 numbered cards (0–9) in four colors (Red, Green, Blue, Yellow).
• 8 “Skip”, 8 “Reverse” and 8 “Draw Two” cards.
• 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four”. | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score at least 500 points over one or more rounds. Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes out. | --- ### Setup 1. Shuffle the full deck face down → create the draw pile. 2. Deal each player 7 cards. Keep them hidden from others. 3. Flip the top card of the draw pile onto the discard pile; this starts the play area. *If the flipped card is an action card (e.g., Skip), apply its effect immediately before anyone plays.* --- ### Turn Order & Play Players take turns clockwise unless a Reverse changes direction. On your turn: 1. **Play a Card** - Must match either: * Color, OR * Number/Action value of the top discard card. - If you have no playable card, proceed to step 2. 2. **Draw One Card** - Take the top card from the draw pile. - If it’s playable, you may use it right away on the same turn. Otherwise keep it and end your turn. 3. **Declare "UNO"** - When you’re reduced to exactly one card, shout “UNO!” before another player takes their turn. Failure to do so results in drawing two penalty cards if caught. 4. **End Turn** - Pass play to the next active player according to current direction. --- ### Action Cards | Card | Effect | |------|--------| | **Skip** | Next player loses his/her turn. | | **Reverse** | Reverses play order (clockwise ↔ counter‑clockwise). In a 2‑player game, acts like Skip. | | **Draw Two (+2)** | Next player draws two cards AND misses a turn. | | **Wild** | You choose the new color to continue play. | | **Wild Draw Four (+4)** | Same as Wild but forces next player to draw four cards and miss a turn. Can only be played if you truly cannot legally play any other card matching the previous color/value. *(See “Challenge” below.)* --- ### Challenges (Optional Rule) When a **Wild Draw Four** is played, the challenged player can call “challenge.” 1. They reveal all remaining hand cards. 2. If they had a legal card of the preceding color, the challenger **loses**: they must draw six cards instead of four. 3. If not, the challenger keeps playing normally while the original player still has to draw four. *(This rule adds strategy—players try to bluff with +4s.)* --- ### Winning a Round A round ends when a player discards her last card (“goes out”). That player scores points equal to the sum of values of all cards still held by opponents: | Card Value | Score | |------------|-------| | Numbers 0‑9 | Face value | | Skip / Reverse / Draw Two | 20 pts | | Wild / Wild Draw Four | 50 pts | The winner of the round receives those points. Then start a fresh round until somebody reaches ≥ 500 total points. --- ### Common Variations | Variation | How It Changes Gameplay | |-----------|------------------------| | **Stacking** | Players may stack multiple `+2` or `+4` cards rather than just drawing once. | | **No Challenge** | Disallow challenges against Wild Draw Fours. | | **“One More”** | After going out, players get one extra turn to finish off any opponent who might still hold low‑value cards. | | **Custom Deck Sizes** | Use fewer/more cards per player or different starting numbers. | Feel free to tweak these rules to suit your group! Enjoy the colorful chaos of UNO.
